edges.reason: Point-to-point shortest-distance language is a helpful model, but perpendicular-shortest distance is a separate fact and not derived merely from the two-point line axiom.
The distance in question is the length of the perpendicular from the point, so perpendicularity identifies which segment is measured.
A distance-defined ellipse supplies a helpful locus analogy. Equal distance to a point and a line defines a parabola independently and does not use a constant distance sum.

The parabola condition equates a point-to-focus distance with a point-to-line distance. Its focal half cannot be stated without knowing that distance between two points is the connecting segment's length.
